- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.3) within 3–5 days, model should adjust downward by 2–5% per day to reflect sentiment-driven sell-off.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when recent 18-day mean is below 75.00 — model tends to overreact.
- If forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in first 3 days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model should not overfit to recent volatility — use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward 70–75 range after 10+ days of high prices, reduce forecast slope by 15–20% for next 5 days.
- Forecast should not exceed 10% above or below 18-day moving average unless sentiment is clearly bullish or bearish.
